ai.title: CLI /run command error handling refactor
ai.summary: handleRunTerminalCommand returns structured {result, stdout, stderr} instead of string. CLI /run prefix now writes stdout/stderr directly on command-not-found, preventing fallback to Claude. Covers npm-app/src/cli.ts and tool-handlers.ts. Tool handler wrapper adapts to new return shape.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to run a command that doesn't actually exist (like typing '/run nonsensecommand'), the program now shows you the error message right away instead of pretending it ran and falling back to a default response. The behind-the-scenes function that executes commands was also changed to package the result, the normal output, and the error output as separate pieces rather than one combined text, and the code that calls it was updated to match. This is live now for the internal tooling and affects anyone triggering command-not-found situations through the /run path.

ai.title: cd command only updates project root in user mode
ai.summary: In `npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts`, the `handleRunTerminalCommand` function now checks `mode === 'user'` before updating the project root via `cd`. This prevents assistant-initiated `cd` commands from persisting working directory changes, restricting root updates to explicit user actions.

eli5.text: When you type a cd command yourself, the app now actually changes your working directory. Before, any cd command from the app itself would also change your directory, which could be surprising. Now only your explicit cd actions update the project root, so the app can still navigate around in the background without affecting your actual location. This affects you whenever you're switching between folders in the project, your manual cd commands will work as expected, and you won't be unexpectedly moved around by the app's internal operations.

ai.title: Add look to skipped terminal commands
ai.summary: Added 'look' to the SKIPPED_TERMINAL_COMMANDS array in common/src/constants.ts. This ensures the 'look' command is excluded from standard processing or execution flows. Scope is limited to core constants.

eli5.text: A command named 'look' is now being skipped along with a handful of other commands that the system intentionally ignores. If you were watching the list of commands that get passed over, you would now see 'look' sitting next to names like 'make' and 'please'. The change affects only the internal list that decides which commands are left alone, so nothing you run every day will start behaving differently.

ai.title: Referral Status API, Banner Component, Landing Page
ai.summary: Referral check logic in common/src/util/server/referral.ts returns structured `ReferralStatus` with stable reason codes (`Referral Limit Reached`, `Referrer Not Found`, `Unknown Error`) and `msg` fields, replacing raw string reasons. The `/api/referrals/[code]` route now calls `hasMaxedReferrals` server-side and returns a `ReferralCodeResponse` including `status`, removing the client-side 401 guard to support anonymous lookups. A new `Banner` component is mounted inside providers in `web/src/app/layout.tsx` with `z-20` to ensure clickability above the `z-10` navbar. `web/src/app/page.tsx` removes `mounted` state hydration checks, replaces `Globe` with `BackgroundBeams`, and simplifies copy layout.

eli5.text: The referral system now reports clearer failure reasons and lets visitors check referral links without signing in. When you look up someone's referral code, the site no longer blocks you with a login prompt and instead returns whether you has hit their referral limit. A small on-screen notice now appears above the top menu so important messages stay clickable. The homepage also swapped its spinning globe graphic for a different background and tidied up how some text is laid out.

ai.title: Fix build errors in env schema and referrals page
ai.summary: Updated `common/src/env.mjs` to simplify `runtimeEnv` and add `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPPORT_EMAIL` to both server and client schemas. Fixed JSX apostrophe encoding in `web/src/app/referrals/page.tsx` to resolve build errors. Changes affect core environment configuration and web referral UI.

eli5.text: You can now contact support using a support email address that both the server and the public-facing side of the app recognize, instead of each guessing at the address independently. When you visit the referrals page and see the 'referral limit' message, the sentence around the apostrophe in "you've" displays correctly rather than showing a broken character. The support email is wired into the app's core environment configuration, and the referrals page text now renders as intended.

ai.title: Add privacy policy and terms of service pages
ai.summary: New web/src/app/privacy-policy/page.tsx and web/src/app/terms-of-service/page.tsx added with full legal text. Footer and navbar updated to link these pages. Home page gains copy-to-clipboard for npm install command and responsive text layout. @tailwindcss/typography added for prose styling of legal content.

eli5.text: You can now read the full Privacy Policy and Terms of Service directly from the website, they show up as new pages linked in the footer and top menu. The homepage also gained a one-click button to copy the install command, so you no longer have to manually select and copy it yourself. These pages use a styling add-on that makes long legal text readable right in your browser. If you visit the site today, you’ll see the new footer links and the copy button on the main page.

ai.title: Pricing page feature list corrections
ai.summary: Moved 'Custom integrations' from the standard tier to the Custom tier in web/src/app/pricing/page.tsx. Removed 'Dedicated AI model' from the Custom tier features array. Internal copy adjustment to align displayed features with actual plan capabilities.

eli5.text: The pricing page now lists different features under each plan. If you visit the page, you'll see that Custom integrations have moved from the standard tier up to the Custom tier, and the Dedicated AI model option has been removed from the Custom tier's feature list. This means the features shown for each plan better match what's actually included.
